What is HTML and what is it used for?

HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the standard markup language for creating web pages and web applications. It describes the structure of web pages using elements represented by tags. HTML is used for structuring content, embedding media (images, videos), creating forms, linking pages via hyperlinks, and providing a foundation for CSS styling and JavaScript interactivity. The current version is HTML5, which introduced semantic elements, native multimedia support, and APIs for complex web applications.

How do you create radio buttons and checkbox inputs in HTML forms?

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<body>
    <form>
        <fieldset>
            <legend>Gender (Radio Buttons - only one selectable)</legend>
            <input type="radio" id="male" name="gender" value="male">
            <label for="male">Male</label>
            <input type="radio" id="female" name="gender" value="female">
            <label for="female">Female</label>
            <input type="radio" id="other" name="gender" value="other">
            <label for="other">Other</label>
        </fieldset>

        <fieldset>
            <legend>Hobbies (Checkboxes - multiple selectable)</legend>
            <input type="checkbox" id="reading" name="hobby" value="reading">
            <label for="reading">Reading</label>
            <input type="checkbox" id="gaming" name="hobby" value="gaming">
            <label for="gaming">Gaming</label>
            <input type="checkbox" id="sports" name="hobby" value="sports">
            <label for="sports">Sports</label>
        </fieldset>

        <input type="submit" value="Submit">
    </form>
</body>
</html>
```

**Radio buttons:**
- Same `name` attribute makes them mutually exclusive
- Only one radio in a group can be selected

**Checkboxes:**
- Can have same or different `name` attributes
- Multiple checkboxes can be selected independently
- Use `<fieldset>` and `<legend>` for grouping related options

What is the difference between GET and POST methods in HTML forms?

```html
<!-- GET method: data appended to URL -->
<form action="/search" method="GET">
    <input type="text" name="q" placeholder="Search...">
    <input type="submit" value="Search">
</form>
<!-- Submitting sends: /search?q=your+query -->

<!-- POST method: data sent in request body -->
<form action="/register" method="POST">
    <input type="text" name="username" placeholder="Username">
    <input type="password" name="password" placeholder="Password">
    <input type="submit" value="Register">
</form>
```

**GET:**
- Data appended to URL as query string (?key=value)
- Visible in browser address bar
- Bookmarkable and cacheable
- Limited length (approx. 2048 characters)
- Use for: searches, filters, read-only operations
- Never use for passwords or sensitive data

**POST:**
- Data sent in HTTP request body
- Not visible in URL
- Not bookmarkable
- No size limitations
- Use for: form submissions, login, registration, file uploads
- Required for sensitive or large data

How do you embed video in HTML5 using the video element with multiple formats, poster image, and controls?

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<body>
    <!-- Basic video with controls -->
    <video width="640" height="360" controls>
        <source src="video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
        <source src="video.webm" type="video/webm">
        <source src="video.ogv" type="video/ogg">
        Your browser does not support the video tag.
    </video>

    <!-- Video with poster image, autoplay, loop, muted -->
    <video width="640" height="360" controls autoplay loop muted 
           poster="thumbnail.jpg">
        <source src="movie.mp4" type="video/mp4">
    </video>

    <!-- Video with custom dimensions and preload -->
    <video width="100%" height="auto" controls preload="metadata">
        <source src="presentation.mp4" type="video/mp4">
        <track src="subtitles_en.vtt" kind="subtitles" srclang="en" label="English">
        <track src="subtitles_es.vtt" kind="subtitles" srclang="es" label="Español">
    </video>

    <!-- Responsive video using max-width -->
    <video controls style="max-width: 100%; height: auto;">
        <source src="responsive-video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
    </video>
</body>
</html>
```

**Video attributes:**
- `controls`: shows play/pause/volume/fullscreen
- `poster`: image shown before video plays
- `autoplay`: starts automatically (often requires muted)
- `loop`: repeats video
- `muted`: starts without sound
- `preload`: `none`, `metadata`, `auto`
- `width`/`height`: dimensions

**Formats:** MP4 (H.264) - best compatibility, WebM, Ogg
- `<track>` adds captions/subtitles with WebVTT files

What is SVG and how is it different from Canvas? Show an example of drawing a circle, rectangle, and text in SVG.

```html

SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics)

Differences: Canvas vs SVG

  • Canvas: Pixel-based (raster), immediate mode, better for games/physics, no DOM elements
  • SVG: Vector-based, retained mode, better for static diagrams, DOM accessible
  • Canvas: Fast for animations, loses quality when scaled
  • SVG: Perfect scaling, each element is a DOM node (can attach events)
``` **Canvas vs SVG:** - Canvas = "drawing" (pixels), SVG = "describing" (XML) - Canvas modifies pixel buffer; SVG modifies DOM - Canvas: better for real-time graphics, games - SVG: better for static graphics, logos, icons, data visualization - Canvas: single element, event handling via coordinates - SVG: each shape is an element, can have onclick directly
